subject: Post-call: latency & volume signals — hosted vs dedicated recommendation
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@fastlane.ai>, Priya Nair <priya@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: latency & volume signals — hosted vs dedicated recommendation

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Short recap + recommended next steps so we have a single place to iterate:  

Key signals you shared (measured from your staging traces):
- Steady-state baseline: ~75 qps across text-generation endpoints during business hours (US PST), average request size 280 tokens.
- Bursts: periodic spikes to ~320 qps for up to 10 minutes (marketing events).
- Latency requirements: p95 generation latency must be <= 180 ms for customer-facing autocomplete flows; background batch jobs can tolerate ~600 ms.
- KV cache hit rate currently ~12% in your prototype setup; you anticipate warming to ~40% once deployed.

Initial recommendation (short):
- Move forward with a hybrid-first approach: Dedicated capacity for steady-state low-latency traffic (p95 target), with a hosted fallback/passthrough for burst overflow to avoid overprovisioning.
- Pilot: 2 dedicated GPU nodes (reserved pool) tuned for small-batch, low-latency inference + hosted API route configured as overflow (token-based throttled).

Rationale:
- Dedicated gives predictable p95 tail and lower unit cost for sustained qps.
- Hosted fallback prevents lost requests during marketing spikes without immediate heavy capital commitment.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Kimberly / Alex: can you review the attached dashboard screenshot and confirm the sizing assumptions (I sketched two node profiles there)? (attached: latency_qps_dashboard.png)
2) Samir: please confirm whether burst traffic is cached-friendly (i.e., repeated prefixes) or largely new prompts — that changes batching & cache benefits.
3) If Fastlane is okay with the pilot profile, we’ll produce a short MAP and an order-of-magnitude pricing estimate.

Attachments: latency_qps_dashboard.png (screenshot), mutual-action-plan_v1.pdf (draft MAP)

Thanks — feel free to reply inline.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
nikhil@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

--
Redwood Inference — inference that scales predictably
From: Samir Gupta <samir@fastlane.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency & volume signals — hosted vs dedicated recommendation

Nikhil — thanks for the clear write-up. A few quick clarifications from our side:  

- Bursts are mostly traffic to the same autocomplete endpoints (high overlap in prefixes) — marketing campaigns trigger many similar requests. That should improve cache hit once warmed.
- The p95 target (<=180 ms) is hard for us to relax — even temporary regressions frustrate internal stakeholders.
- Procurement: Fastlane prefers monthly reserved capacity commitments to start, but we need an internal finance nod before we can do 12-months.

Agree with the hybrid pilot. Can you include fallback SLA behaviour in the MAP (what happens when hosted is used for overflow — any throttling, cost deltas)?

Also looped in ops-tech@fastlane.ai for any network/VPC questions.

—Samir
VP Product, Fastlane AI
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Samir Gupta <samir@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency & volume signals — hosted vs dedicated recommendation

Thanks Samir — good detail. A couple of technical clarifications and an ask from engineering:  

Technical notes:  
- If bursts are cache-friendly (high prefix overlap), effective p95 for dedicated nodes will improve materially once KV caching is warmed (we assume move from 12% -> 40% as Nikhil wrote). That supports the 2-node piloting assumption.
- For Dedicated nodes: we’ll tune for small-batch micro-batching (batch size 8-16 depending on model); request coalescing and lower tail latency kernels are enabled.
- Hosted overflow behaviour: we recommend a graceful degradation policy — route overflow to a slightly smaller model variant (same tokenizer/format) with documented delta in quality; include automatic roll-back to hosted default if error rate increases. We’ll capture those behaviors in the MAP with clear observable gates.

Engineer ask: Alex — can you prepare a short perf matrix showing p95 vs qps for (a) 2-node dedicated, (b) 3-node dedicated, and (c) hosted fallback at 250 qps and 500 qps? Aim to surface expected unit-cost, and expected tail latency under cache-warm and cache-cold states. I’ll include that matrix in the MAP.

Samir — we’ll get that back to you within 48 business hours. In meantime, can you confirm procurement timeline (target to sign pilot order)?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick replies — circling back with concrete next steps so we keep momentum:  

1) Alex will deliver the perf matrix (2-node / 3-node / hosted overflow) by EOD Tuesday.
2) I’ll push an updated MAP (includes fallback SLA, cost ranges, provisional pilot SOW) to the shared doc and send the HubSpot deal link.
3) Samir / Priya: please confirm target internal sign date for a month-to-month pilot (we suggested ~June 14). If that works we’ll reserve the pilot pool for the second week of June.

If we get finance approval for the monthly pilot, we can start with a 30-day reserved pool and then convert to a quarterly/monthly reserved commit if utilization justifies it.

Thanks — will follow up after Alex posts the matrix.

Best,
